summary: The mechanism holds on current master (7e12891): both CUDA kernels read the gate columns (row bytes 2560..4607) only in the epilogue, after a cold-L2 flush, and nothing earlier touches those lines. The expected gain (~+0.6-1.0% headline) is inside the +/-1.5% CI, so the run will be read from the per-row deltas. Two build-text fixes are needed before it runs: use the kernel's own R = B*TOK, and define the helper only once.
justification: Plausible. On master the sliding_cluster_kernel reduce-scatter (qkv + b*stride + (HQ+2HKV)*D + h*D + d0) and splitkv_attn_sk_kernel finalize_store read the bf16 gate only after the DSMEM merge or the ticket merge. TASK.md says every timed replay starts with a cold L2, and the q/k/v loads (cluster prologue, or the separate _pre_attention_kernel on the sk routes) touch only the first 2560 B of each 4608 B row. So the gate lines really are cold. The row is 36x128 B and the gate offset is 20x128 B, so each head's 64 bf16 are exactly one 128 B line and the line math in the change is right. The sk-kernel merge goes through ticket atomics and fences, so the compiler cannot hoist the gate load above it. That leaves ~0.5-0.8 us of HBM latency on the last CTA's critical path, which matters on the latency-bound rows (sliding decode_1 cluster 10.8 us of 11.9; sliding verify_1 PSEUDO 10.0 of 13.2; full decode_1 two-level 19.0 of 22.4). Full decode_16/32 stream 328-655 MB through a ~50 MB L2, so flat is right there. Correction against current master: sliding decode B=17..32 now routes through splitkv_attn_sk_kernel with PSEUDO and TOK=1 (the [sd] window route, profile shows sk kernel 14.0 us at decode_32), not cluster C=4. The decode_32 expectation still applies, but through the sk prefetch, and only if R is B*TOK. Weakest link: the sliding decode_1 cluster epilogue. Inside the post-barrier reduce-scatter block, nvcc may already have scheduled the gp[0]/gp[1] loads ahead of the 16 DSMEM map_shared_rank reads and the Ls/o merge, hiding part of the latency. Then the most leveraged row (~0.85% headline per us) gains well under 0.3 us. Checking SASS for the LDG position relative to the DSMEM loads would settle it before the run. Magnitude: the whole expected headline gain is below the CI floor, so the run is readable only per row.
confounders: restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master (landed ~15:20Z, after the hypothesis was written against eb1b68b): sliding decode B=17..32 is now chosen at prepare time between sk window (TOK=1) and the cluster C=4 incumbent, with a 1.03x head-to-head gate. The change speeds up both candidates, so it can flip that route. A decode_32 delta could then be a route flip, not the prefetch. The audit must confirm 'PATH CHOSEN: sliding decode B=17..32: [pre-attn + stream-K sk window]' as on master, a line missing from the hypothesis's log checklist.

restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn: its gates (C=16 at B=1, C=4 cluster vs Triton, PSEUDO verify B=1 >= 1.05x vs FA3) are timed at prepare. The prefetch only helps the CUDA side, so it can only strengthen those routes, but a route that flips to CUDA where master used Triton/FA3 would confound the row. The listed PATH CHOSEN / [slide-gate] ROUTE checks cover this.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket: in the two-level ticket, the CTA that runs finalize_store is chosen at runtime. The grid-wide prefetch loop covers that because every CTA prefetches before the early returns. No interaction beyond that, and the effect does not depend on how the ticket is tuned.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / v2 stream-K at 1<B<=64: same kernel, but the KV stream evicts the prefetched lines. Expect flat, plus 32-64 KB of extra reads. A loss there would point to perturbed code generation (registers or scheduling) in the shared template, not the mechanism.
interference: No companion. The submit is scored and the change is one hint instruction in two kernels with no route, math or grid change. The attribution comes from the per-row deltas, which the expected list already pins: sliding decode_1 (cluster only), sliding verify_1 (PSEUDO TOK=8), full decode_1 (two-level), sliding decode_32 (sk TOK=1). The full decode_16/32 rows serve as a built-in null, since the same template gets the prefetch but L2 thrashes. The only real ambiguity is a route flip, and the PATH CHOSEN log lines settle that for free. An ab-revert of a landed hypothesis would remove the very kernels being edited, and a control that splits the two kernels would cost a second scored run to separate two effects that already show up on disjoint rows. Leaving it uninterpreted costs less than a companion.
rules_flags: No rules problem: prefetch.global.L2 is a hint with no data dependence. It adds no host sync, caches nothing across calls, changes no precision, attends every key as before and stays graph-capturable.

Build-text bug to fix before running: the change says R = PSEUDO ? B*8 : B. On current master the kernel uses R = PSEUDO ? B*TOK : B. Copied literally, the TOK=1 sliding-decode instantiations (variants 6/7, B<=32) would prefetch qkv rows B..8B-1, past the end of the tensor. Prefetch should not fault, but those lines are wasted HBM traffic, possibly from other allocations. Reuse the kernel's existing R (compute it before load_prefix, or move the existing const R line up).

Duplicate definition risk: _SKF_CUDA is '#include ...' + _SK_CUDA[:'template <int STAGES, bool TICKET'] + skF code. With prefetch_l2 defined above that slice point (required), a second copy of the helper in the skF source would cause a redefinition compile error and silently drop the skF build. Define it exactly once, in _SK_CUDA above the slice point, plus once in _SLIDE_CUDA (a separate module).
open_questions: Does the SASS of sliding_cluster_kernel already issue the gate LDGs before the DSMEM merge loads (cuobjdump -sass on the built module)? If so, the decode_1 row should be expected flat and the headline gain drops to ~0.3-0.5%.

Does the extra prologue code change the [slide] fp8qk register, local or spill line (master 124 regs / 32 B local), or the [sk]/[sd]/[ps] regs lines for the PSEUDO variants? A new spill would cancel the gain on exactly the rows meant to improve.

At full decode_1 (~20 MB of KV in 19 us), do the 16 prefetched gate lines survive in L2 until the two-level finalize? If they are partly evicted, full decode_1 reads flat while the sliding rows (0.5 MB window) still gain.

Is the v_scale_p prefetch in the cluster kernel worth keeping? The last rank already __ldg's v_scale_p at kernel start, so it is probably warm for every rank by the epilogue. It is harmless either way.
